artifactText: {"schemaVersion":1,"findings":[{"id":"sql-injection-customer","title":"SQL injection through customer query parameter","severity":"high","location":"Lines 8-10: `/invoice` builds `sql` with `req.query.customer` and passes it to `db.query`.","evidence":"Line 9 interpolates untrusted input directly into SQL: `WHERE customer = '${req.query.customer}'`. An attacker-controlled quote can alter the query structure.","repair":"Use the database driver's parameterized-query API, for example `db.query('SELECT id, total FROM invoices WHERE customer = ?', [req.query.customer])`, with the placeholder syntax appropriate for the configured driver. Validate the parameter is a string of expected length.","confidence":"high"},{"id":"path-traversal-download","title":"Path traversal in download path construction","severity":"high","location":"Lines 14-16: `/download` joins `DATA_ROOT` with `req.query.name` and sends the resulting file.","evidence":"Line 15 uses `path.join(DATA_ROOT, req.query.name)` without verifying that the resolved result remains inside `/srv/app/downloads`. Inputs such as `../../...` can escape the intended directory after normalization.","repair":"Resolve the requested path and enforce containment before sending: compute `const root = path.resolve(DATA_ROOT); const file = path.resolve(root, String(req.query.name));` and reject unless `file.startsWith(root + path.sep)`. Prefer an allowlisted file identifier rather than accepting a path.","confidence":"high"},{"id":"command-injection-diagnostics","title":"OS command injection through diagnostics host","severity":"critical","location":"Lines 19-23: `/diagnostics` interpolates `req.body.host` into a shell command passed to `exec`.","evidence":"Line 20 constructs `ping -c 1 ${req.body.host}` and passes it to `exec`, which invokes a shell. Shell metacharacters in the request body can add or alter commands.","repair":"Do not construct a shell command from request input. Use `execFile` or `spawn` with fixed arguments, for example `execFile('ping', ['-c', '1', validatedHost], callback)`, and strictly validate `validatedHost` as an IP address or constrained hostname before invocation.","confidence":"high"}],"summary":"The source exposes three direct injection paths: SQL injection in invoice lookup, path traversal in file download, and critical shell command injection in diagnostics. Replace string interpolation with parameterized or argument-based APIs and enforce input validation and path containment."}
